sDescription: Taylor Swift achieved a No. 1 on the US Hot 100 with the 10:13 extended edition of 'All Too Well,' setting a record as the longest track to lead the chart. Don McLean previously held this record starting in 1972, when his 8:36 song 'American Pie' reached the top position.

Country singer Blake Shelton was selected as People magazine's "Sexiest Man Alive". Within the 32-year history of the annual feature, he became the second musician to be given this title, following Adam Levine, who is his fellow coach on The Voice and received the honor in 2013.

Taylor Swift held the No.1 position on the US album chart with her fifth studio album, 1989. Opening-week sales for 1989 in the US marked the highest total for any album since 2002, and the release emerged as the top-selling album of 2014 in the US. Globally, the album has achieved sales exceeding 9 million copies.

An independent review recommended leaving copyright terms unchanged, resulting in an unsuccessful effort by Sir Cliff Richard to extend the duration musicians receive record royalties. Richard sought a 95-year copyright term instead of the existing 50-year period. In 2008, copyright protection for Sir Cliff's first major hit, "Move It"—recorded in 1958—was set to begin expiring.

Defence contractor David H. Brooks, a multimillionaire, secured New York's Rainbow Rooms and booked the preferred performers of his daughter Elizabeth for her coming-of-age bat mitzvah celebration. The line-up of appearing stars featured 50 Cent, Tom Petty, Aerosmith, Don Henley, Joe Walsh, and Stevie Nicks. Receiving a $500,000 payment for his appearance, 50 Cent delivered a four-song set, which included the adapted lyric, "Go shorty, it's your bat miztvah, we gonna party like it's your bat mitzvah". With an estimated total cost of $10 million, the event factored in expenses for corporate jets used to transport the artists to and from the location.

Tony Meehan, drummer with The Shadows, died at the age of 62 due to head injuries following a fall at his London flat located in Maida Vale. He achieved the 1963 UK No.1 single 'Foot Tapper' along with 28 additional UK Top 40 singles. In 1961, he departed from The Shadows to pursue session drumming work alongside Joe Meek. Additionally, he secured the UK No.1 hit 'Diamonds' in collaboration with Jet Harris.

Financial figures published by The Rolling Stones revealed that the group earned £175 million in gross revenue from the 2002 '40 Licks World Tour.' Additionally, the report indicated that their earnings surpassed $1 billion between 1989 and 2002 through tour income, album sales, and royalties.

The funeral of INXS vocalist Michael Hutchence was interrupted by a supporter who attempted to jump from a 20-foot balcony with a cord tied around his neck. Police intervened and transported him to a psychiatric facility.
John Squires, the former guitarist of Stone Roses, debuted his new band The Seahorses live at The Buckley Tivoli in England for an audience of 200 fans.

A Zoroastrian priest led the funeral service for Freddie Mercury, which was attended by 35 family members and close friends, including Elton John along with the remaining members of Queen. Cremation for Mercury took place at Kensal Green Cemetery in West London, England.

Bon Jovi were at No.1 on the US singles chart with 'You Give Love A Bad Name', it peaked at No.14 in the UK. Released as the first single from the album Slippery When Wet, in 2009 it was named the 20th-greatest hard rock song of all time by VH1.

Lionel Richie reached No. 1 in the US with 'Truly'. As a writer and co-writer, Richie secured a No. 1 hit every year from 1978 to 1986 with 'Three Times A Lady', 'Still', 'Lady' (Kenny Rogers), 'Endless Love' (Diana Ross), 'All Night Long', 'Hello', 'Say You, Say Me', and We Are The World.

Press advertisements alleging that 'home taping was wiping out music' were published by the British Phonographic industry. Cliff Richard, 10cc, Elton John and the Boomtown Rats supported this campaign.

20 Golden Greats by Glen Campbell started a six-week run at No.1 on the UK album chart. During his 50 years in show business, Campbell released more than 70 albums and has sold over 45 million records.

George Harrison released All Things Must Pass which includes the hit singles 'My Sweet Lord' and 'What Is Life', as well as songs such as 'Isn't It a Pity' and the title track that had been turned down for inclusion on releases by the Beatles. The triple album would go on to be certified 6x Platinum by the RIAA, making it the best selling album by a solo Beatle.

Black Sabbath, Cactus, and Steel Mill (which featured Bruce Springsteen) performed at the Sunshine In located in Asbury Park, New Jersey. Each of the three acts performed two shows, with tickets priced at $5.00.

While on a North American tour, the Rolling Stones performed the opening concert of a four-night run at Madison Square Garden in New York City. Across the four evenings, the band drew an audience of 55,000 attendees and brought in a gross of more than $100,000.

The 16-date UK package tour with Jimi Hendrix, Pink Floyd, The Move, The Nice, The Outer Limits, The Eire Apparent and Amen Corner travelled to Belfast to appear for two shows at the Whitla Hall, Queens College. It was Jimi's 25th birthday and before the shows, the guitarist was given a birthday cake by the promoters This was to be the only concert that The Jimi Hendrix Experience ever played in Ireland.

A court in Tettenhall, Staffs issued Mick Jagger a £16 fine for driving infractions. During the proceedings, his solicitor stated to the court: "The Duke of Marlborough had longer hair than my client and he won some famous battles. His hair was powdered, I think because of fleas. My client has no fleas."

The Beatles recorded their inaugural BBC radio session at the Regent Street BBC Paris studio in London, performing 'Twist and Shout', 'Love Me Do', and 'P.S. I Love You'. These recordings were subsequently broadcast on the BBC Light Program titled 'Talent Spot'.

Neil Christian and the Crusaders performed a concert at Holloway Women’s Prison in London, England, with a young Jimmy Page playing guitar. The inmates wore homemade mascara crafted from burnt match charcoal and were all dressed in faded floral print dresses of washed-out red, blue, green, and yellow.

British singer Oritsé Williams is best known as the founding member of the boy band JLS, who finished as runners-up to Alexandra Burke on the fifth series of The X Factor in 2008. The group's first two singles, 'Beat Again' and 'Everybody in Love', both reached No. 1 on the UK Singles Chart. Before disbanding in December 2013, JLS sold over 10 million records.

Stephen Manderson is an English pop artist, rapper, singer, and songwriter who performs under the stage name Professor Green or simply Pro Green. His 2010 second single, 'Just Be Good to Green', featured British singer Lily Allen and reached the top 5 in the UK.

English rapper, singer-songwriter, musician, and record producer Mike Skinner is known as The Streets and secured a 2004 UK No.1 album with A Grand Don't Come For Free. Skinner has additionally put out music under his own name, in the group D.O.T. alongside frequent collaborator Rob Harvey, and utilizing the pseudonym The Darker the Shadow the Brighter the Light.

Twista, also known as Tung Twista and born Carl Terrell Mitchell, is a US rapper who was once recognized as the fastest rap delivery artist in the world. He achieved a US No. 1 album in 2004 with Kamikaze and a US No. 1 single with Slow Jamz.

American singer, guitarist, and songwriter Myles Kennedy serves as the lead vocalist and rhythm guitarist for the rock band Alter Bridge, as well as for Slash featuring Myles Kennedy and the Conspirators.

Fiachna O'Braonain is a member of the Irish rock band Hothouse Flowers, which achieved a No.11 single in the UK in 1988 with 'Don't Go'. The group's debut album, People, came out in 1988 and stands as the most successful debut record in Irish history, claiming the top spot in Ireland in just one week and later peaking at No.2 on the UK Albums Chart.

Wallis Buchannan performed with Jamiroquai, a group that achieved a UK No.1 album in 1993 with Emergency on Planet Earth and a UK No.1 single in 1998 with 'Deeper Underground'. The band has received a Grammy Award in 1998 and attained worldwide sales of more than 26 million albums.

American musician Charlie Benante is primarily known for playing drums in the thrash metal band Anthrax and the crossover thrash band Stormtroopers of Death. Anthrax is regarded as one of the pioneering groups of the 1980s thrash metal movement.

Mike Bordin is the drummer of the American rock band Faith No More. Their version of The Commodores song 'I'm Easy' became a hit single in 1993, reaching No. 3 in the UK and No. 4 in the US. The band also released the best-selling albums The Real Thing in 1989 and Angel Dust in 1992.

Calvin Hayes was a member of the British band Johnny Hates Jazz, which achieved international success and a No.5 single on the UK chart in 1987 with 'Shattered Dreams'. The single also reached No.2 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent one week at the top of Billboard's Adult Contemporary chart. Hayes passed away at the age of 63 on 10th July 2026, following a collapse at his home in Washington.

Ashley Ingram is a singer in the English trio Imagination, which scored a UK No. 2 single in 1982 with 'Just An Illusion'. The group achieved hits across 28 countries and collected four platinum discs, nine gold discs, and upwards of a dozen silver discs globally from 1981 to 1983.

Charlie Burchill is the guitarist for the Scottish rock band Simple Minds. The group achieved a 1985 US No.1 single with 'Don't You, Forget About Me' and a 1989 UK No.1 single with 'Belfast Child', along with more than 20 additional UK Top 40 singles. In 2016, they received the British Academy's Ivor Novello Award for Outstanding Song Collection.

Randy Brecker was a member of the American jazz-rock band Blood Sweat & Tears. The group achieved a US No. 2 single in 1969 with "Spinning Wheel" and a US No. 12 single in 1969 with "You've Made Me So Very Happy". Their second album, Blood, Sweat & Tears, reached No. 1 in the US in 1968.

sDescription: Trevor Davis played in the British pop/rock band Dave Dee, Dozy, Beaky, Mick and Tich, which achieved a UK No.1 single in 1968 with 'Legend Of Xanadu'. Following a short illness, Davis passed away in hospital on 13th January 2015.

American guitarist, singer, and songwriter Jimi Hendrix. Hendrix moved to England in late 1966, after bassist Chas Chandler of the Animals became his manager. He had the 1967 UK No.6 single 'Hey Joe', the 1970 UK No.1 single 'Voodoo Chile', and his third and final studio album Electric Ladyland (1968) peaked at No.1 in the US. Hendrix who is widely considered to be the greatest guitarist in musical history, made appearances at the 1967 Monterey Pop Festival, the iconic 1969 Woodstock Festival and the 1970 Isle Of Wight Festival. He was one of the first guitarists to make extensive use of tone-altering effects units in mainstream rock, such as fuzz distortion, Octavia, wah-wah, and Uni-Vibe and was the first musician to use stereophonic phasing effects in recordings. Hendrix died on 18th September 1970 after choking on his own vomit.

Eddie Rabbitt was a singer and songwriter known for his 1981 US No. 1 hit "I Love A Rainy Night". His compositions were recorded by Elvis Presley, Dr Hook, and Tom Jones. Rabbitt passed away from cancer on May 7th, 1998.

Buzz Cason was an American singer, songwriter, and record producer. He helped establish The Casuals, which was Nashville's initial rock and roll band. Working alongside Leon Russell as a session musician, Cason produced The Crickets's rendition of 'La Bamba'. Additionally, he provided backing vocals for Elvis Presley as well as Kenny Rogers. Cason passed away in Franklin, Tennessee, on 16 June 2024 at 84 years old.

French music producer and songwriter Henri Belolo co-created musical acts such as The Ritchie Family and Village People alongside Jacques Morali. He passed away on 3 August 2019 in Paris, France at the age of 82.

Al Jackson was an American songwriter, producer, and drummer. As a founding member of Booker T. and the MG's, the house band for Stax Records, he contributed to the 1962 US No. 3 single 'Green Onions' and the 1969 UK No. 4 single 'Time Is Tight'. Known for his drumming skill, he was affectionately called "The Human Timekeeper". Throughout his career, Jackson collaborated with numerous performers, such as Rufus Thomas, Al Green, Carla Thomas, Eddie Floyd, Sam & Dave, Otis Redding, Elvis Presley, Bill Withers, Wilson Pickett, Leon Russell, Jerry Lee Lewis, Eric Clapton, Aretha Franklin, and blues guitarist Albert King. On October 1st, 1975, Jackson was shot and killed by burglars inside his home.
